data.title: append_comment — collision-resistant note ID
data.summary: One-line fix: replace f'n{len(notes)+1}' with f'n-{datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc):%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%f}' in _append_comment.

sections.body: Current code in reckon/mcp.py _append_comment: note_id = f'n{len(notes) + 1}'. This collides when: (a) a note is deleted and a new one appended — both get id 'n1'; (b) two agents read the same plan (both see len=0) and both append — both get 'n1'. The id is used as a key in comments dicts in state.js; collision silently overwrites the earlier note.

Replace the single line with: note_id = f'n-{datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc):%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%f}'. Format: n-20260526T162100123456. Sortable lexicographically (= chronologically). Human-readable. Microsecond resolution; collision probability is negligible given that write_plan's atomic rename costs > 1ms.
In tests/test_mcp_tools.py: test_append_comment_note_id_format (id starts with 'n-'; format matches r'n-\d{8}T\d{6}\d{6}'), test_append_comment_note_id_unique (two rapid calls produce distinct ids).
